subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Why Rocky Planets Differ
description: Learn Why Rocky Planets Differ in one minute.

hook.text: Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars formed from the same dust cloud. Why are they so different today?

buildup.text: Distance from the Sun set starting temperatures. Closer planets got more heat, changing what could form.

discovery.text: Size matters most. Larger worlds hold thicker atmospheres, which trap heat and enable liquid water.

twist.text: Venus and Earth started nearly identical. A runaway greenhouse on Venus shows how fragile the balance is.

climax.text: Mars was too small to keep its air. Mercury too close and tiny. Only Earth hit the sweet spot.

punchline.text: Same dust, different distances. Four worlds, four fates.

quiz.question: What is the most important factor that made the rocky planets so different?
options: Their size and distance from the Sun
The order in which they formed
The number of moons each planet captured

details.summary: Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars all formed from similar materials in the inner solar system, yet they're radically different today. Their divergent fates result from differences in size (affecting atmosphere retention and geological activity), distance from the Sun, magnetic field strength, and…
details.whyItMatters: Understanding why four rocky planets diverged so dramatically is essential for predicting habitable conditions on rocky exoplanets.
takeaways: Four rocky planets formed from similar materials but diverged completely
Size determines atmosphere retention, geological activity, and magnetic fields
Habitability requires the right combination of many planetary properties

faq.question: Why did Mars lose its atmosphere while Earth kept one?
faq.answer: Mars is only 11% of Earth's mass — too small to maintain a strong magnetic dynamo. Without a global magnetic field, solar wind gradually stripped Mars's atmosphere over billions of years.

faq.question: Why does only Earth have plate tectonics?
faq.answer: Earth's unique combination of size, internal heat, water content, and crustal composition enables plates to subduct. Venus is similar in size but too hot and dry for plate tectonics.
